source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or China-diversification framing found in available Sun Pharma FY24-25 disclosures. Company describes itself as a global specialty generics player with backward-integrated API manufacturing (14 API units) reducing third-party supplier dependence, but this was not explicitly tied to China diversification in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: APIs (largely petrochemical/fermentation-derived) reportedly contribute roughly 6% of company revenue via captive/backward-integrated manufacturing; no specific raw-material-cost-to-crude linkage percentage was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export/international business (US, Emerging Markets, Rest of World, Global Specialty) was approximately 67% of FY24-25 consolidated revenue (India domestic ~33%), implying substantial foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy text was located in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found confirming Sun Pharma as a named beneficiary of the Indian government's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs (PLI 1.0 beneficiaries publicly identified are other companies); Sun Pharma's own AR/press materials were inaccessible to confirm either way.

china_plus_one.evidence: IKS Health is a US-healthcare-focused KPO/IT-services provider (medical documentation, coding, billing support for US physician enterprises); no China exposure or China+1/supply-chain diversification narrative found in available sources — not applicable to this business model.

inr_exposure.evidence: Multiple secondary sources (Screener-derived geography data, IPO/company profiles) consistently report International (USA) revenue at 100% and Domestic (India) revenue at 0%; company platform serves physician enterprises in the US, Canada and Australia with 'a focus on the US markets' and over 90% of revenue from the US specifically.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention found; IKS is a services/KPO company, not a manufacturer, so India's PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme is not applicable.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's API and CDMO businesses reflect alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification and CDMO outsourcing; the company's API Plus business and new 'Global Technical Operations' (GTO) function (unifying manufacturing, supply chain and procurement, using the Kinaxis platform) are positioned as 'ensuring secure global supply chains and elevating India's stature in the global API and CDMO landscape' — described by secondary sources as aligning with the broader 'China plus one' trend, but no explicit quantified revenue attribution to China+1 was found in available excerpts.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources note Lupin's gross margin improved (to ~68.4% in Q1FY25) partly due to backward integration in its API/generics cost base, but no specific raw-material-cost-to-revenue percentage was found in accessible excerpts.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 geography mix disclosed as US 36%, India 34%, RoW 24%, API 5% of global sales (US FY2025 sales ~USD 925 Mn vs USD 815 Mn in FY2024); a Q1FY25 earnings discussion referenced 'Forex' as a line item affecting expenses alongside Mirabegron settlement, R&D and M&A costs, but the specific hedging policy text could not be retrieved directly.

pli_scheme.evidence: Multiple secondary sources identify Lupin (alongside Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's, Cipla, Aurobindo) as among Indian pharma companies that have used the government's PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs to invest in domestic API manufacturing; no specific PLI-linked revenue percentage was disclosed in accessible excerpts.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived commentary notes 'export demand, particularly in off-highway components and software services, has also increased' for FY2024-25, but no explicit China+1 or supply-chain-diversification framing was found in available sources; primary AR PDF (bosch.in, NSE archives, BSE) could not be fetched directly (all returned HTTP 403), so this may be incomplete.

govt_capex.evidence: FY2024-25 revenue growth (8.1% to INR 18,087 crore) was attributed partly to increased sales in the 'off-highway segment' (construction/agriculture equipment components, tied to infrastructure/capex-linked demand) alongside Mobility Aftermarket growth; no explicit government-capex revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses foreign exchange forward contracts and foreign currency option contracts to hedge foreign currency exposure relating to firm commitments and highly probable forecast transactions; derivatives are used exclusively for hedging, not trading/speculation.
inr_exposure.evidence: Notes to financial statements (per third-party financial-data aggregator summary): 'The Company uses forward exchange and currency option contracts to hedge against its foreign currency exposures relating to firm commitments and highly probable forecast transactions.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch Limited was among 75 companies (67 under 'Component Champion' category) that secured PLI approval under the Auto/Auto-Components PLI scheme (Component Champion Incentive Scheme) announced March 15, 2022; government began disbursing incentives under the PLI-Auto scheme from Q4 FY25 onward. No company-specific revenue/benefit percentage disclosed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: IHCL is a domestic hospitality/hotel operator (Taj Hotels) with international presence across ~13 countries via owned hotels and management contracts, but no China+1/manufacturing supply-chain diversification narrative applies to this business; no such language found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL/Taj operates hotels across four continents and 13 countries (per company press materials), implying some foreign-currency revenue and forex exposure, but no quantified USD revenue share or hedging policy details could be retrieved in this session.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative was found for Alkem in accessible sources. Press coverage of FY25 results attributes non-US international growth (10.5% of FY25 sales, +28.2% YoY in Q4) to 'robust double-digit growth in Australia and key European markets' without any China+1 framing. Separately, a third-party summary described Alkem's raw-material sourcing as 'primarily from domestic Indian suppliers supplemented by imports from key global partners in the United States, Germany, and Spain, while maintaining low direct exposure to high-risk regions like China' -- a supply-resilience point, but not an explicit AR-stated China+1/order-diversification narrative tied to revenue growth.

rural.evidence: No official rural revenue % disclosure was located. A third-party profile (Forbes India) states Alkem's trade generics business (correlated with rural/Tier-2/Tier-3 distribution, sold via retailers/distributors rather than physician promotion) was roughly Rs2,400 crore of ~Rs8,100 crore domestic revenue in FY23 (~30%), and describes distribution in rural markets as a long-standing company strength; this is not a figure sourced from the annual report's MD&A itself.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: CFO Nitin Agrawal stated in a subsequent (FY26) earnings call that Alkem hedges approximately 80% of its ForEx exposure and monitors raw material prices closely; this was not independently verified against the FY24-25 AR's own hedging-policy note.
inr_exposure.evidence: US sales contributed 19.4% of FY25 total sales (up from prior-year base); non-US international contributed a further 10.5%, together 29.8% international vs 70.2% domestic. CFO quote on ~80% hedge ratio is from an earnings call, not confirmed directly against the AR text.

pli_scheme.evidence: No explicit statement was found confirming Alkem's participation in the Government of India's PLI (bulk drug/API) scheme, despite Alkem being a large-scale domestic API manufacturer (notably cephalosporin API). Could not verify beneficiary status or any associated revenue/incentive % from accessible sources; treat as unconfirmed rather than a definitive non-participation.

china_plus_one.evidence: NH is a domestic hospital services provider, not a manufacturer/exporter of goods. No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative was found; the company's 'diversification' language in investor materials refers to overseas medical-tourism expansion (Cayman Islands hospital, and post-FY25 UK acquisition), not China+1 sourcing.

rural.evidence: Investor materials mention NGO-partnered free medical camps and telemedicine (200,000+ remote consultations) extending reach into rural areas, and the hospital network includes Tier-2/3 cities (Mysore, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati, Jamshedpur), but no explicit rural revenue percentage is disclosed in sources reviewed.

govt_capex.evidence: Management commentary (FY25-27 outlook) cites 'better pricing from government scheme patients' (e.g., PMJAY/Ayushman Bharat empanelment) as a growth/margin lever, but no percentage of revenue from government schemes was disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No floating-rate debt percentage disclosure found for FY2024-25. Note: NH's later Practice Plus Group (UK) acquisition, completed Nov 2025 (i.e. FY2025-26, after this report's period), was financed with SONIA-linked floating-rate debt (~200bps + SONIA) — that is outside the FY2024-25 reporting window.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cost of materials consumed (medical/surgical consumables, pharmaceuticals, implants) was approximately Rs 1,170.1 Cr against consolidated revenue of Rs 5,516.3 Cr in FY25 (~21.2% of revenue). This is medical-consumables cost, not crude-oil-linked raw material.

inr_exposure.evidence: Consolidated FY25 revenue included Health City Cayman Islands operating revenue of ~Rs 11,829 Mn against consolidated operating revenue of ~Rs 54,830 Mn (~21.6%); Cayman Islands dollar is pegged to USD, making this effectively USD-linked revenue. Company also reported ~$86.8 million foreign-currency-denominated debt as of March 31, 2025. No specific hedging policy was found in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI (Production Linked Incentive) is a manufacturing-sector scheme; not applicable to a hospital/healthcare-services provider, and no disclosure of PLI benefit was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Q4 FY25 earnings call: international sales made up ~55% of revenue; Q1 FY26 call noted the company began supplying the BSUK brand directly from its Indian plant to the European market with repeat orders, and is targeting new markets like Saudi Arabia. No explicit 'China+1' or supply-chain-diversification-from-China framing was found in accessible sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Usha Martin's wire rope products serve mining, infrastructure, crane and elevator end-markets which have indirect linkage to government infrastructure/mining capex cycles, but no specific revenue percentage tied to government capex was disclosed in sources accessible.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Earnings calls (Q1 FY25/FY26) referenced ongoing 'debt reduction' but no floating-vs-fixed rate borrowing split was found in accessible sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Usha Martin divested its captive steel-making business (including iron ore and coal mines at Barajamda/Jharkhand) to Tata Sponge Iron/Tata Steel in 2019. Post-divestment, the company's key raw material is purchased wire rod/steel, implying exposure to external steel/wire-rod price movements rather than direct captive mining or crude oil cost pass-through; no specific raw-material cost percentage was disclosed in sources accessible.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export sales were reported at approximately 55% of total revenue in FY25 (Q4 FY25 earnings call), spanning US, European (via BSUK, UK), Middle East (Saudi Arabia targeted) and other markets, implying meaningful foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD-denominated revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed in sources accessible.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative found in available sources. Exports (~8% of sales, ~100 countries incl. rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reported at ~Rs 868 crore as of March 2025 (up from ~Rs 749 crore in March 2024) per secondary financial data sources; no breakdown of floating vs. fixed-rate borrowings was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials cited are grain, ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass bottles, described as volatile cost items pressuring gross margins; no explicit tie to crude oil or petrochemical input pricing was found in sources accessed, so this is not treated as crude exposure per the stricter definition.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (roughly 8% of total sales value) span US, Canada, Europe and Southeast Asia across ~100 countries and ~63 duty-free outlets; no specific hedging/forward-contract policy was found in sources accessed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure of PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme participation or benefit was found in sources accessed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Nippon Life India AMC is a domestic asset management (mutual fund) company with no export/manufacturing business; no China+1 narrative applies.

rural.evidence: NIMF's AUM from 'Beyond the Top 30 cities' (B-30) stood at Rs 1.32 trillion (USD 14.9 billion), up 15% YoY, forming 19.8% of NIMF's AUM vs. 18.6% for the Industry (as of March 31, 2025).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has an Offshore Business & Gift City AUM segment (Rs 15,246 Cr as of Mar 2025) but no disclosed % of revenue in USD or hedging policy was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party brokerage/analyst summaries note NFIL's Specialty Chemicals/CDMO exports serve global majors (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) and a ~Rs 540cr capex for an agri-intermediate project for 'a global major', while also noting China has massive chemical overcapacity and is 'aggressively dumping generic agrochemical intermediates into the global market at dirt-cheap prices' (a headwind, not a China+1 tailwind). inr_exposure.evidence: Company 'generates a majority of its revenue from outside India' with exports reportedly ~77% of revenue in Q4FY25 (quarterly, not confirmed full-year FY25 figure), implying material USD/foreign-currency exposure. pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found that NFIL is a named beneficiary of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for specialty/fluorochemicals; only general policy-level mentions of a prospective PLI for the chemicals sector were found, not company-specific participation.

crude_exposure.evidence: Per FY25 result-update figures (ICICI Direct research summary), raw material expenses were approx Rs 2,776 crore on revenue of Rs 11,516 crore (~24.1% of revenue); not confirmed as specifically crude-oil/petrochemical linked, likely general API/intermediate input costs.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of Torrent Pharmaceuticals as a PLI (bulk drugs/API) scheme beneficiary was found in available sources; company is primarily a branded formulations/generics player rather than a bulk-drug/API-focused manufacturer typically cited under the PLI KSM/API scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Phoenix Mills is a domestic Indian real estate operator (malls/retail, office, residential, hospitality) with no export business; no China+1 narrative applies.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure of PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme participation or benefit was found for JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals in the sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' or supply-chain-diversification-from-China framing was found in available secondary sources (press releases, analyst notes) covering Zydus Lifesciences FY24-25; the company's export narrative centers on US generics market-share gains (US Formulations ~50% of consolidated revenue, up ~24-31% YoY) rather than explicit China+1 positioning. inr_exposure.evidence: Per Zydus Lifesciences Q4/FY25 results commentary (company press release, referenced via secondary sources): FY25 revenue mix was approximately US Formulations 50%, India Formulations 25%, Consumer Wellness 14%, and Europe & Emerging Markets (LatAm, Asia Pacific, Africa) 11% of consolidated revenue -- indicating roughly half of consolidated revenue is USD-denominated (US Formulations business). pli_scheme.evidence: No direct confirmation found that Zydus Lifesciences is a named approved applicant under the Government of India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/medical devices in the sources accessible; Department of Pharmaceuticals' approved-applicant list was referenced but specific company names (including Zydus) were not surfaced in available search results. Could not verify via AR notes directly.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD&A states: 'Amid geopolitical instability and global trade restrictions...the Company swiftly activated contingency plans to ensure operational continuity. It diversified sourcing and logistics strategies, established alternative shipping routes...' and separately, in the strategy section: 'Aligned with our diversification strategy, we are expanding our focus beyond our prominent markets in North America and Europe...seeking opportunities in the fast-growing markets of Asia, specifically India, China and the rest of Asia...to achieve a balanced geographical diversification in our revenue.' This is general supply-chain/geographic diversification language rather than an explicit 'China+1' framing crediting Western OEMs shifting sourcing away from China for revenue/order growth; note the company itself also operates a manufacturing plant in China.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated Note 48 Interest rate risk exposure: Variable rate borrowings INR 134.63 million, Fixed rate borrowings Nil, Total borrowings INR 134.63 million as at 31 March 2025 (31 March 2024: Variable INR 2,330.58 million, Fixed Nil) - all borrowings are variable/floating rate.
